name: heavy-baritone-ledger-drawl
idea: The closest parody: a heavy-set Brooklyn man in his mid-twenties, deep round baritone with a slight wheeze between lines, relaxed in tone but landing every syllable precisely on the beat, dry and close to the mic. Music asked for as a short tag list: late-90s New York boom bap around 88 BPM, a sparse hard kick-and-snare with long gaps, one dark minor-key loop, a scratch or two between rules. The rapper says each 'Number ...' himself, punched like a count-off, so the countdown feel comes from the delivery, not a sample. Exclude singing and melodic vocals.

name: old-gravel-mob-accountant
idea: A different performer: a man in his fifties with a gravel-and-cigarette rasp, half-rapped, half-spoken, deadpan like a mob bookkeeper reading the books aloud to a new recruit, unhurried and menacing, a smirk audible on the jokes. Ask for the music in prose, as a scene: a smoky back room, a lone muted-trumpet and upright-bass loop over dusty, slow, heavy drums, tape hiss, the beat dropping out for the last two lines so 'No hand on the printer.' lands dry. Mafioso-era East Coast rap mood, nothing modern.

name: queens-woman-hard-snare
idea: A woman MC instead: low, husky alto from Queens, tough and amused, clipped staccato delivery that bites every rhyme word, with a small crew of male voices answering the numbers in the background (parentheses). Music asked for as a production spec: hard compressed drum break, snapping snare, minor-key horn stab on every new rule, deep sub bass, mid-90s grit. Confident, swaggering, like she is teaching the class.

name: hungry-young-debut-register
idea: A young, hungry nineteen-year-old rapper in a higher, slightly nasal register, voice still raw at the edges, eager and fast, pushing the beat and running out of breath at line ends. Ask for the music with technical gear words: 12-bit sampler crunch, swung MPC drums at 92 BPM, filtered bassline, chopped dusty piano stab, vinyl crackle, mono-ish early-90s mix. Raw demo-tape energy rather than polished album sound.

name: radio-countdown-promo
idea: Built as a late-night New York radio countdown bit, nodding to the beat's own origin as a radio promo: a smooth, mellow, almost whispered deep male MC raps the rules, while a separate brash radio-DJ voice shouts each 'Number one / four / six / seven / ten' like a chart countdown. Ask for the music as a station segment: a looping dark keys riff, crisp boom-bap drums, a short rising sci-fi countdown blip before each number, radio compression on the DJ voice only. Two clearly different voices, the MC never sings.

name: noir-strings-spoken-sermon
idea: A tall, slow, preacher-deep bass voice from Brooklyn delivering the rules like commandments from a pulpit, almost spoken word, heavy pauses, each number intoned with weight and a dry joke underneath. Music asked for cinematically: a minor-key film-noir string loop and low cello, a slow head-nod drum with a big dry snare, church-hall reverb only on the numbers. Cold, authoritative, a lesson from someone who already watched it all go wrong.
